title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study (verifier‑consistency estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline)
abstract: Preregistered estimand and scope: this study (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) asks whether a deterministic validator treats identical canonical LLM candidates differently under two scoring conditions when the same candidate is reused for both conditions (preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate"). We executed the frozen plan on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a single canonical generation per task from the declared model gpt‑5‑mini. Exact archived evidence (execution/execution_manifest.json; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) shows baseline = 120/120 verifier passes and guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared seed) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (1) publish the full byte‑for‑byte artifact bundle and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints (execution/execution_manifest.json), (2) use those artifacts to diagnose why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a degenerate paired contingency (identical canonical candidates + deterministic validator), and (3) provide artifact‑grounded runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed sampling, validator diversification, and task‑heterogeneity expansion) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question NetOps practitioners typically require (independent generative reliability). The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is a central NetOps function whose correctness is safety‑critical: transient misordering, incorrect ACLs, or unsafe switchover sequences can cause outages or security breaches. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) are commonly used to certify proposed configurations before deployment, providing an auditable oracle for correctness checks [Brown et al., 2023]. Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate intent translation, but their stochastic generation raises questions about operational reliability: what is the probability that an independently sampled LLM candidate will satisfy verifier constraints? To address this, we preregistered study CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 to compare a deterministic template baseline to an LLM generator under frozen confirmatory semantics. Critically, the preregistration specified a particular estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) and a generation semantics—shared_initial_candidate—whose operational interpretation differs from the independent‑sampling question operators often want. This paper (i) reports the exact, audited confirmatory outcome grounded in archived artifacts; (ii) documents why the preregistered design produced a degenerate paired contingency; and (iii) supplies deterministic, artifact‑anchored modifications to answer independent generative reliability while preserving reproducibility.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation. Offline semantic validators such as Batfish and related control‑plane analyzers enable pre‑deployment checks that detect reachability, ACL, and routing policy violations from static device configurations; they are an operationally accepted safety step for configuration changes [Brown et al., 2023; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent work couples LLM generation with verifier checks in a generate–validate–repair loop; empirical studies emphasize that (a) repair budgets and orchestration design strongly influence end results and (b) most repair gains accrue early in bounded repair loops. Methodological axes across the literature that materially affect inference are: sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs. independent per‑condition sampling), repair budget semantics (single‑pass vs. bounded iterative repair), and validator scope (syntactic vs. semantic multi‑property verifiers). Our contribution is not a new verifier or model but a preregistered, artifact‑anchored diagnosis of how a specific confirmatory design maps to a precisely archived estimand and why that mapping matters for operational interpretation.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The experiment was preregistered before any model outputs (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...; stored in the artifact bundle). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired binary difference in verifier pass rates across N = 120 tasks). Confirmatory design: paired binary analysis with shared_initial_candidate semantics—one canonical LLM generation per task (seed_0) was produced and reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforced per‑task required_sequences and workflow_policies and emitted full JSON traces per episode (execution/scoring/*.json). Model and orchestration: declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). Execution accounting: planned_episode_count = 240, completed_episode_count = 240, model_calls_used = 120 because a single canonical generation was produced per task and reused for both conditions—this accounting is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and the provider call traces (execution/provider_calls/*) and shared response files (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt) are archived with SHA‑256 fingerprints (representative: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be...). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation (binary pass requires satisfying all required commands and transient constraints encoded in the task manifest). Analysis: paired_binary_analysis_v1 with bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test as preregistered.
sections.results: Archived confirmatory counts and deterministic traces. All confirmatory episodes completed (see execution/execution_manifest.json). Outcome: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120; paired contingency n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Point estimate for paired difference = 0.00; bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative validator traces demonstrate deterministic validation of template‑aligned required_sequences: e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json records parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, normalized_configuration equal to the shared canonical candidate, and validation_after.valid = true. Why the contingency is degenerate (artifact‑visible cause). Two archived, preregistered design choices created the deterministic collapse: (A) generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (a single canonical candidate per task was produced and reused for both scoring conditions); (B) task templates encode explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies that the canonical candidate was constructed to satisfy. Because the validator is deterministic, identical inputs necessarily yield identical pass/fail outputs; the full provider traces and response files (execution/provider_calls/* and execution/responses/*) show the same canonical candidate was scored under both conditions for every pair. Artifact‑grounded runnable modifications. The archived pipeline permits immediate, deterministic reruns answering the independent generative‑reliability question by changing only the generation semantics: (1) independent_per_condition rerun—generate separate seeds per condition (baseline seed_i, guarded seed_j) and rescore with the same validator; (2) multi‑seed confirmatory design—draw K≥3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (3) validator diversification—score candidates with an independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. All code, seeds, and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints required for deterministic reruns are included (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and operational implications. The confirmatory statistics correctly address the preregistered estimand—verifier‑consistency under identical inputs—but do not answer the deployment question practitioners usually require: the independent probability that an LLM, when sampled independently, will produce a verifier‑passing configuration. That operational estimand requires independent per‑condition sampling or multi‑seed replication. Our artifact bundle makes it trivial to perform those reruns deterministically and reproducibly. Threats to validity (artifact‑identified). Internal validity: shared_initial semantics removed generation variance by design and therefore cannot estimate independent generative reliability. Construct validity: tight task templates and a single deterministic validator increase the chance that template‑aligned canonical candidates pass deterministically, limiting generalization to open natural language intents. External validity: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generality across model families and production topologies. Contamination and exposure: preregistered string‑overlap heuristics reported no flags under chosen thresholds (analysis/contamination_summary.csv), but absence of a flag is not a formal proof of zero training‑data exposure; full provider call traces and response hashes are archived so external auditors can run deeper exposure analyses off‑bundle. Runnable next steps (artifact paths). To estimate independent generative reliability with the archived artifacts: change generation_semantics to independent_per_condition and run the driver that consumes execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/model_configuration.json (both archived). The canonical candidate files (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt) and per‑episode scoring traces (execution/scoring/*.json) document the original shared‑candidate run and are the precise files to replace in the rerun.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment and released exhaustive byte‑for‑byte artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition passed the deterministic validator on all N = 120 tasks (120/120 each); paired difference = 0.00 with a degenerate bootstrap CI of [0.00, 0.00]. Archived provider call traces, shared canonical candidate files, and per‑episode validator JSON traces show that identical candidates were scored in both conditions—this deterministic reuse is the artifact‑visible reason for the degenerate paired contingency. The confirmatory result therefore answers the preregistered verifier‑consistency estimand correctly but does not estimate independent LLM generative reliability. We supply artifact‑grounded, deterministic rerun protocols (independent_per_condition, multi‑seed, validator diversification) that convert the design into an informative operational comparison without sacrificing reproducibility. All artifacts required for exact reproduction—including the immutable initial master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the published bundle to support audit and follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and producing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not part of the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
